messages:
mira: Quick heads-up — after enabling per-layer mixed-precision (FP8 for most layers, INT8 on a few mid layers) on the canary, we're seeing ~9% regression in p99 tail latency at batch_size=8. Posting profiler snippet below, looks like cast/dequant paths spiked.

alex: Can you paste the profiler output and the config you used? Which kernels are now dominating time?

mira: Profiler summary from the canary run (recent):
```
TIME   %    kernel
120ms  42%  attention_fp8_kernel
52ms   18%  dequant_kernel (quant->fp32 casts)
30ms   10%  memcpy_h2d / memcpy_d2h
26ms    9%  kv_cache_lookup
20ms    7%  softmax_fp8
12ms    4%  lm_head_fp32
```
Notes: embedding and lm_head were explicitly excluded (left FP32). The kernel selector logged 2 per-layer fallbacks (layer 10) flagged as "calib_overflow" which inserted extra cast paths. memcpy time also higher than baseline.

sam: Did the selector fallback because calibration flagged saturation? Or is it a kernel mismatch on sequence length?

mira: Selector flagged overflow on calibration for a few weight quant buckets — fallback path used fp32 kernels for attention in that layer which caused extra conversions in the execution graph (hence dequant spikes). Calibration was run with default sample set (n=128).

jen: Calibration size could be the issue — too small or not diverse enough. Iʼve seen transient overflows go away with 256+ diverse sequences. Also, what about batching heuristics? Any changes there?

alex: Canary had a change: max_batch_tokens was bumped 1024->2048 to increase throughput. That increases average seq_len per batch and makes KV reuse patterns change (less frequent identical-prefix hits). With larger batches, more memory copies for KV and longer warmups. That can raise tail.

mira: Repro command I used: 
```
./run_perf.sh --model=redwood-3b --quant=fp8,partial_layers="2-5,10-12" --exclude="embedding,lm_head" --batch_size=8 --max_batch_tokens=2048 --calib_samples=256
```
Profiler raw above.

sam: Quick plan: run two controlled variants:
A) Force quant path (disable selector fallback) but pin kernel-selection thresholds to ignore tiny overflow deltas (test risk).
B) Keep selector safe but mark sensitive layers (10,11) as FP32 and re-run. Compare p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU memcpy times.

perf-bot: benchmark queued (job id 7753). Expected finish ~15m.

alex: Also suggest lowering max_batch_tokens back to 1024 and reduce batch timeout to 8ms for the canary to see if tail improves — batching params can amplify casting overhead by increasing heterogeneous sequences in a batch.

mira: Agreed. I'll: 1) add lightweight selector logging that emits why a fallback happened (overflow vs unsupported instruction) and per-layer time contribution; 2) schedule the two variants A/B; 3) run with max_batch_tokens=1024 and batch_timeout=8ms.

jen: FYI excluding embedding/lm_head gave a small quality improvement on regen tests but almost no perf benefit — expected since those are tiny relative to attention kernels. Quality tradeoff is fine.

ops-bot: Reaction :thumbsup: (mira created branch "selector-logs/partial-quant")

alex: Ping @sam when results land — if p99 remains up we may opt for conservative rollout (mark sensitive layers fp32) until calibration + selector fixes are in.

mira: Will post follow-up with perf-bot results and a diff of selector logs. Thanks all. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
